title: U.S. House · New York's 17th Congressional District
area: Lower Hudson Valley, covering Rockland and Putnam counties and parts of Westchester and Dutchess counties, north of New York City.

context.text: Cait Conley won the June 23, 2026 Democratic primary over Beth Davidson, Effie Phillips-Staley, John Cappello, and Mike Sacks, 49.5% to 31.8% and lower totals for the others. Phillips-Staley separately won the Working Families Party primary but subsequently withdrew from the November general-election ballot; Conley is the WFP nominee as well as the Democratic nominee. Incumbent Michael Lawler advanced unopposed on the Republican and Conservative Party lines after his primary was canceled.

Lawler defeated then-incumbent Sean Patrick Maloney 50.3% to 49.7% in 2022 (under different district lines) and won re-election 52.1% to 45.8% in 2024, the same year Kamala Harris carried the district 49.9% to 49.3%. As of September 22, 2026, all four major forecasters (Cook Political Report, Decision Desk, Inside Elections, Sabato's Crystal Ball) rated the general election a "Toss-up." As of June 30, 2026, Lawler had raised $8.17 million to Conley's $4.32 million.

summary.text: Michael Lawler is the incumbent U.S. Representative for New York's 17th Congressional District, elected in 2022 after two years in the New York State Assembly. He sits on the House Financial Services Committee and the House Foreign Affairs Committee.

background.text: Born in Suffern, New York; earned a bachelor's degree in business administration from Manhattan College in 2009.

Worked as a staffer for Westchester County Executive Rob Astorino, as executive director of the New York Republican State Committee, and as deputy town supervisor of Orangetown before serving in the New York State Assembly (2021-2023).

priorities.text: Campaign material emphasizes constituent service and a record he describes as bipartisan, citing additional funding for law enforcement and first responders, tax relief for middle-class families, and funding increases for Hudson Valley schools he says he secured in the state Assembly.
priorities.quote: In the Assembly, that meant additional funding for law enforcement and first responders, tax relief for middle class families, and historic funding increases for our schools in the Hudson Valley.

priorities.text: Says he has opposed New York City congestion pricing as a tax on Hudson Valley commuters.
priorities.quote: Led the fight against Gov. Hochul's absurd congestion pricing plan – a $5,000/year commuter tax on hardworking Hudson Valley families just trying to get to work

positions.summary: Has campaigned against Manhattan congestion pricing as a policy imposed on Hudson Valley commuters and taxpayers.

Official issues page says he helped introduce bipartisan legislation to extend the enhanced ACA premium tax credits and signed a discharge petition for a clean 3-year extension; it also says he supports work requirements for able-bodied adults without young children in Medicaid.
positions.quote: After my own party leadership refused to move a bipartisan bill, I signed a discharge petition to force a vote on a clean 3-year extension of the credits.

record.text: Serves on the House Financial Services Committee (Capital Markets and Housing and Insurance subcommittees) and, in the 119th Congress (2025-2026), chairs the House Foreign Affairs Committee's Middle East and North Africa Subcommittee and also sits on its Western Hemisphere Subcommittee.
Represented the 97th District in the New York State Assembly from 2021 to 2023 before his election to Congress.

summary.text: Cait Conley is a U.S. Army veteran and former White House National Security Council and Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency official running as the Democratic and Working Families Party nominee for NY-17. She won the June 23, 2026 Democratic primary in a five-way field.

background.text: Earned a bachelor's degree from the U.S. Military Academy at West Point and master's degrees from MIT and Harvard University.
Served 16 years in the U.S. Army; later served on the White House National Security Council and at the Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency (CISA) during the Biden administration.

priorities.text: Campaign website lists education investment (affordable childcare, universal pre-K, capping student-loan interest rates, opposing voucher programs) and rebuilding aging infrastructure as priorities.

positions.summary: Opposes voucher programs, saying they strip funding from public education.
Supports increasing access to affordable childcare through federal subsidies and tax credits and investing in universal pre-K.
Campaign policy page calls for letting everyone opt in to a public insurance option and for defending the Affordable Care Act and Medicaid.
positions.quote: Allowing everyone to opt in to a public insurance option, regardless of age, expanding coverage, and driving down costs across the marketplace. Defending the Affordable Care Act & Medicaid and expanding Medicare to include vision, dental, and hearing.

positions.summary: Campaign policy page calls for passing Roe v. Wade into law, including access to abortion, contraception and IVF.
positions.quote: Passing Roe v. Wade into law to restore a woman’s right to make personal healthcare decisions without interference from politicians — including access to abortion, contraception, and IVF.

positions.summary: Campaign policy page calls for reining in ICE with body cameras and a mask ban, revoking 287(g) agreements, and focusing enforcement on dangerous criminals rather than long-standing community members.
positions.quote: Reining in ICE and restoring accountability, requiring body cameras, standard law enforcement uniforms with visible ID, and prohibiting masked agents. Revoking 287g agreements so that local police can focus on protecting their own communities.

positions.summary: Campaign policy page calls for expanding federal investment in solar, wind and geothermal projects and for rejoining the Paris Climate Agreement.
positions.quote: Investing in clean energy, expanding federal investments in solar, wind, and geothermal projects.

positions.summary: Campaign policy page calls for cutting outdated red tape and zoning rules that slow housing projects.
positions.quote: Making it easier to build affordable housing by cutting outdated red tape and zoning rules that slow down projects and drive up prices.

positions.summary: Campaign policy page calls for universal background checks, closing the loophole for unlicensed dealers, and federal grants to help states adopt red-flag laws.
positions.quote: Passing Universal background checks to protect lawful gun owners while stopping criminals
